Information
The battle of Cotais took place in either 552 or 553 (most likely 553). Little is known about the battle but we do know that it was mostly a cavalry battle won by the sassanids under Khosrow I. The byzantine commander is still unkown.
Background
in 552 (or 553) the sassanids were in need of responding to the current losses and therefor sent a force to confront a small byzantine army. The battle was a cavalry battle and it is likely that the more skilled Sassanid cavalry won thanks to their experience that the byzantines lacked and the flat terrain making it easy to fight.
The Battle
The battle was won by the superior sassanid cavalry. It was thanks to a surprise counter-attack that the sassanids were able to send the byzantine force routing. The persians had more faster and skilled cavalry such as the Zhayedan (Elite sassanid cavalry also nicknamed "Immortals"), Grivpanvar and Aswaran while the byzantines used more heavy and simple cavalry such as the clibanarii and koursorses. The byzantines were able to hold the sassanid force for a while but eventually broke down and routed due to the Sassanids overwhelming archery and cavalry battle skills.
